chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all together, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the lead (dirhams) bought with the silver (dirhams), he (peace be upon him) said: 'If the lead was predominant upon it, so there is no problem with it'.

key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no problem with it

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on buying lead dirhams with silver dirhams if the lead is predominant?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the rules of *bay' al-fadl* (exchanging unequal quantities of the same commodity) regarding lead (*usurb*) and silver, establishing that if lead is the dominant component, the exchange is permissible. It reflects the Shia juristic principle that the 'dominant' nature of the commodity determines the validity of the transaction, distinguishing it from strict equal-weight requirements in other contexts. This ruling is foundational in Usuli fiqh for understanding currency exchange (*sarf*) and commodity trading.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, altogether, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abdul Rahman Bin Al Hajjaj,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding the lead (dirhams) bought with the silver (dirhams). He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If the lead was predominant upon it, so there is no problem with it’.
en.sarwar: 15. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and Muhammad ibn ‘Isma’il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from all from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who has said the following:
“About the case of buying al-Asrub with silver, abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘If al- Asrub is more prevalent then it is not unlawful . 555
